name: Cloudflare Workers for Platforms

modes.label: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
modes.note: Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/workers-for-platforms/platform/pricing/: $0.02 per additional million CPU-ms => $0.072 per CPU-hour (cpu_basis active: CPU time = wall time x utilisation); $0.30 per additional million requests => start_fee $0.0000003 (one session = one request); memory not billed. Isolate limits (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/): 128 MB memory, WfP pricing page: max 30 s CPU per invocation (15 min per Cron Trigger/Queue consumer), unlike standard Workers Paid (default 30 s, up to 5 min). Duration/wall time not billed.

modes.label: Dynamic Workers (Worker Loader isolates), Workers Paid plan
modes.note: Requires Workers Paid ($5/month minimum per account; includes 10M requests + 30M CPU-ms, shared with normal Workers). $0.002 per unique Dynamic Worker (Worker ID + code) per day beyond 1,000/month; .load(code) without ID = 1 per invocation. Requests $0.30/M, CPU $0.02/M CPU-ms incl. isolate startup. Limit: 4 distinct Dynamic Workers in flight per Worker request, 10 per Durable Object. Changelog 2026-03-24 'open beta'; docs no longer show a beta label. Could alternatively be its own card.

plans.name: Workers for Platforms
plans.note: $25/month incl. 20M requests ($6.00 at overage rate) + 60M CPU-ms ($1.20) + 1,000 scripts; extra scripts $0.02 each (not modelled). included_usd = $7.20.

plans.name: Workers Paid (Dynamic Workers)
plans.note: $5/month minimum per account; 10M requests ($3.00) + 30M CPU-ms ($0.60) included; 1,000 Dynamic Workers/month included (~$2 at $0.002) not encoded in included_usd.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: Isolates, not VMs: 128 MB memory, one thread; workloads needing more RAM are ineligible.
One estimator session = one request; CPU billed on CPU time only (cpu_util x wall time), wall-clock/idle not billed.
Per-script fee ($0.02 beyond 1,000 scripts) not modelled.

Dynamic Workers (Worker Loader) are priced separately on the Workers Paid plan ($5/month): 1,000 unique Dynamic Workers/month included then $0.002 per Dynamic Worker per day, plus Workers Standard requests ($0.30/M beyond 10M) and CPU ($0.02/M CPU-ms beyond 30M, including isolate startup time). See additions.
Dynamic Workers concurrency: only 4 distinct Dynamic Workers can have in-flight requests per parent Worker request (10 per Durable Object); many concurrent sandboxes need fan-out across requests/DOs.

WfP bills 1 request across dispatch Worker -> user Worker -> outbound Worker; CPU is charged across all three. Custom per-customer CPU/subrequest limits can be set in the dispatch Worker (spend-control lever). Script limit is unlimited (billing $0.02/script beyond 1,000).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: However, the contents of `/tmp` are not persistent and are unique to each request.
snapshot_auto.note: WfP user Workers are stateless V8 isolates invoked per request; there is no machine state to checkpoint. Durable state lives in bindings (KV, D1, R2, Durable Objects). (Sandbox SDK/Containers also lose all state on sleep: 'Containers restart after inactivity or failures'.)

snapshot_on_demand.quote: The Workers Virtual File System (VFS) is a memory-based file system
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API for Workers isolates. Differs in Sandbox SDK: createBackup()/restoreBackup() snapshot a sandbox directory (disk only, no memory) to R2 and can restore into a sandbox later (sandbox/api/backups).

harness_api.quote: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - WfP exposes an API to deploy/dispatch/manage customer-authored Workers (scripts), not a first-party API that drives a coding-agent harness (prompt/stream events/follow-ups) inside the sandbox. No such API is documented anywhere in the Workers or Workers for Platforms docs.

egress_allowlist.quote: Create, allow, or block lists for hostnames requested by user Workers.
egress_allowlist.note: Via an Outbound Worker (code you write, runs outside the user Worker) that intercepts every fetch() from user Workers; enabling it disables connect() TCP sockets. Caveat from the same page: 'Outbound Workers do not intercept fetch requests made from Durable Objects or mTLS certificate bindings.' Programmable, so any URL-based rule (incl. IP-literal hosts) is possible. Sandbox SDK differs: declarative allowedHosts/deniedHosts with hostnames, IPs and CIDRs, enableInternet=false.

egress_http_rules.quote: **Modify requests** - Add authentication headers or transform requests before they leave your platform
egress_http_rules.note: Outbound Worker receives the full Request (method, URL, headers, body) and can block/modify it in code. Sandbox SDK outbound handlers likewise ('denying specific HTTP requests').

ingress_rules.quote: **Runs platform logic** - Executes authentication, rate limiting, or request validation before customer code runs
ingress_rules.note: User Workers are invoked only through your dynamic dispatch Worker (env.DISPATCHER.get), which is the entry point for all requests and can authenticate/route/reject. Plus standard Cloudflare zone controls (WAF etc.). Sandbox SDK preview URLs carry a token in the hostname.

guest_firewall.note: V8 isolates: no kernel, no root, no iptables/nftables. (Sandbox SDK containers: not documented.)

secret_proxy.quote: Configure authentication to your APIs behind the scenes (without end developers needing to set credentials).
secret_proxy.note: Programmable: the Outbound Worker (your code, outside the user Worker) holds secrets and adds headers to any intercepted fetch(); user Worker never sees them. HTTP fetch only (TCP connect() disabled; Durable Object fetches not intercepted). Dispatch Worker can also pass capabilities (RPC stubs) so credentials stay in the dispatcher. Sandbox SDK has the same pattern explicitly: 'Securely inject credentials ... they can hold secrets that the sandbox itself never sees' (outboundByHost).

volume_attach.quote: The Workers Virtual File System (VFS) is a memory-based file system
volume_attach.note: No disks/volumes for Workers; storage is via bindings (R2, KV, D1, Durable Objects), not filesystem mounts. Sandbox SDK differs: mountBucket() mounts R2/S3-compatible buckets as a filesystem (s3fs/FUSE), optionally readOnly.

volume_shared.quote: The Workers Virtual File System (VFS) is a memory-based file system
volume_shared.note: No mounted filesystem exists to share between Workers; shared state is via bindings (APIs), consistent with the card's own feature_evidence.volume_shared note.

isolation.quote: Workers run in V8 isolates rather than containers or virtual machines
isolation.note: Workers for Platforms dispatches requests to user Workers, which are V8 isolates (128 MB memory, one thread each; see card's own isolation field 'isolate').

image_oci.quote: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - WfP user Workers are JS/Wasm code deployed via the Workers API, not machines booted from a Docker/OCI image. (Cloudflare's separate 'Containers' product supports container images, but that is not this product.)

anti_bot.quote: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - WfP is a multi-tenant serverless isolate dispatch platform for running customer code, not a browser/stealth automation product. Cloudflare Bot Management is a separate WAF-side product, not a WfP sandbox feature.

captcha_solving.quote: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no browser or CAPTCHA-solving capability documented for Workers/Workers for Platforms.

egress_ip_type.quote: Create, allow, or block lists for hostnames requested by user Workers.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound fetch() traffic from user Workers egresses through Cloudflare's shared global edge network (anycast datacenter IPs), not a dedicated static or residential IP; card confirms static_egress_ip=false and public_ipv4=false.

own_agent_api.quote: User Workers (V8 isolates), per request + CPU-ms
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - WfP has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product or API of its own; it only runs customer-authored Workers.

mcp_server.quote: cloudflare / mcp-server-cloudflare Public ... MCP servers ... deploy and manage resources on the Cloudflare developer platform
mcp_server.note: Cloudflare ships official MCP servers (mcp-server-cloudflare monorepo, plus docs-linked Observability and Builds MCP servers) that let MCP clients like Claude manage Workers/Workers for Platforms resources (deployments, logs, builds) via natural language.

lang_python.quote: Python Workers Overview ... The pywrangler CLI tool - To run a Python Worker locally, install packages, and deploy it to Cloudflare, you use pywrangler
lang_python.note: Python is a supported Workers language (via Pyodide) and can be deployed as a user Worker under Workers for Platforms, same runtime/dispatch mechanism.

open_source.quote: workerd, Cloudflare's JavaScript/Wasm Runtime ... Apache-2.0 license
open_source.note: workerd, the open-source (Apache-2.0) runtime that executes Workers, is what Workers for Platforms dispatches user code into; the runtime core is open source though the managed WfP control plane/dispatch service itself is not self-hostable.

hipaa.quote: HIPAA - The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) sets the standard for protecting sensitive patient data. Contact your account team to request the HIPAA AoC.
hipaa.note: HIPAA Assurance/BAA is available for Cloudflare (Enterprise), covering the Cloudflare platform including Workers/Workers for Platforms; requires contacting an account team.

eu_data_residency.quote: The Data Localization Suite (DLS) is a collection of tools that enable customers to choose the location where Cloudflare inspects and stores data ... Regional Services - Comply with regional restrictions by choosing which Cloudflare data centers are allowed to decrypt and process your HTTPS traffic.
eu_data_residency.note: Enterprise-only paid add-on (Data Localization Suite / Regional Services) lets customers restrict processing/keys/logs to EU data centers; applies at the Cloudflare account level covering Workers traffic.

max_session_h.quote: There is no hard limit on duration for HTTP-triggered Workers. As long as the client remains connected, the Worker can continue processing, making subrequests, and streaming a response body.
max_session_h.note: Not a VM/session concept: each invocation is a stateless per-request isolate execution. Wall-clock duration is uncapped while the client stays connected (waitUntil() extends up to 30s after response); CPU time is capped separately (WfP: 30s CPU per invocation, 15 min for Cron/Queue triggers) but that is compute billing, not a session-length stop.

persistent_disk.quote: The Workers Virtual File System (VFS) is a memory-based file system... However, the contents of `/tmp` are not persistent and are unique to each request.
persistent_disk.note: User Worker isolates have no durable filesystem; the only writable path (/tmp) is memory-based and scoped to a single request. Durable state must go through bindings (KV/D1/R2/Durable Objects), not a disk.

snapshot.quote: A given isolate has its own scope, but isolates are not necessarily long-lived. An isolate may be spun down and evicted for a number of reasons... Workers are fundamentally preemptible (unlike containers or VMs).
snapshot.note: No checkpoint/snapshot API exists for isolates; there is no VM/container image to snapshot in the first place.

pause_resume.quote: An isolate may be spun down and evicted for a number of reasons: Resource limitations on the machine. A suspicious script... Individual resource limits.
pause_resume.note: Isolates are transparently evicted/recreated by the runtime with no user-facing pause/resume control and no state preserved across eviction (state lives only in external bindings).

fork.quote: V8 orchestrates isolates: lightweight contexts that provide your code with variables it can access and a safe environment to be executed within.
fork.note: There is no process/VM concept to fork; a Worker is JS/Wasm code invoked per-request in isolates the platform creates and destroys itself. No fork API is documented anywhere in the Workers/WfP docs.

fork_running.quote: V8 orchestrates isolates: lightweight contexts that provide your code with variables it can access and a safe environment to be executed within.
fork_running.note: Same isolate model as `fork`: no live-instance forking primitive exists for Workers.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Instead of creating a virtual machine for each function, an isolate is created within an existing environment. This model eliminates the cold starts of the virtual machine model.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No memory-snapshot-based fork/restore mechanism; isolates aren't VMs and have no addressable memory image to snapshot/fork.

docker_inside.quote: The layer 2 sandbox uses Linux namespaces and `seccomp` to prohibit all access to the filesystem and network... Cloudflare can (and does) use a totally empty filesystem (mount namespace) and uses `seccomp` to block absolutely all filesystem-related system calls.
docker_inside.note: V8-isolate JS/Wasm code has no OS/syscall access at all, so it cannot spawn or run Docker/containers inside it.

nested_virt.quote: In Cloudflare Workers, tenants are isolated from each other using V8 isolates — not processes nor VMs.
nested_virt.note: No hardware virtualization exposed to user code; isolates cannot run hypervisors or nested VMs.

root.quote: Currently, Workers does not allow any access to the local filesystem. Therefore, Cloudflare does not expose a filesystem API at all. No API means no access.
root.note: There is no OS/kernel underneath user code to have root on; only sandboxed JS APIs are exposed.

ssh.quote: The layer 2 sandbox also totally prohibits network access. Instead, the process is limited to communicating only over local UNIX domain sockets to talk to other processes on the same system.
ssh.note: No shell/OS process exists to SSH into; a Worker is JS/Wasm executed inside a V8 isolate with no exposed network listener other than the HTTP handler contract.

desktop.quote: V8 orchestrates isolates: lightweight contexts that provide your code with variables it can access and a safe environment to be executed within.
desktop.note: Plainly outside the product: a headless JS/Wasm request-handler isolate has no display server or desktop environment.

browser.quote: Currently, Workers does not allow any access to the local filesystem... Today, Workers are allowed to talk to the rest of the world only via HTTP — both incoming and outgoing.
browser.note: No browser runtime inside the isolate (Cloudflare's separate Browser Rendering product remotely controls headless Chromium elsewhere; it isn't a browser running inside the Worker/WfP isolate itself).

computer_use.quote: V8 orchestrates isolates: lightweight contexts that provide your code with variables it can access and a safe environment to be executed within.
computer_use.note: No GUI/OS surface for computer-use style control; product is a request-scoped JS/Wasm execution sandbox.

custom_image.note: Deployment unit is a bundled JS/Wasm script up to 64 MiB, not a container/VM image; there is no custom base-image mechanism for Workers/WfP.

volumes.quote: The Workers Virtual File System (VFS) is a memory-based file system that allows you to read modules included in your Worker bundle as read-only files, access a directory for writing temporary files...
volumes.note: No disk/volume attach mechanism; storage is exclusively through bindings (R2/KV/D1/Durable Objects), matching the existing feature_evidence.volume_attach=false entry on the card.

public_ipv4.quote: Workers functions run on Cloudflare's global network - a growing global network of thousands of machines distributed across hundreds of locations... a single instance of the runtime can run hundreds or thousands of user-defined applications.
public_ipv4.note: Isolates share Cloudflare's anycast edge; there is no per-Worker/customer dedicated public IPv4 address (inbound is via *.workers.dev / custom domains routed through Cloudflare's shared network, not a dedicated IP).

static_egress_ip.quote: Create, allow, or block lists for hostnames requested by user Workers.
static_egress_ip.note: Outbound traffic controls are hostname/URL based (Outbound Workers), not IP-based; no dedicated/static egress IP is offered for outbound fetch() from Workers/WfP (outbound requests originate from Cloudflare's shared edge IP ranges).

agent_harnesses.quote: Build a multi-tenant platform that runs untrusted code in secure, isolated sandboxes.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Workers for Platforms is a dispatch/isolation layer for running your own customers' JS/Wasm Workers; there are no preinstalled/templated coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) for this product. Cloudflare's separate Sandbox SDK / Containers product has agent-related tutorials, but that is a different product from WfP's V8-isolate dispatch.

gpu.note: Workers isolates are CPU-only JS/Wasm sandboxes with a 128 MB memory cap; no GPU attach exists for this product (GPU inference on Cloudflare is via separate Workers AI, not exposed to arbitrary WfP user code).

windows.quote: Instead of creating a virtual machine for each function, an isolate is created within an existing environment. This model eliminates the cold starts of the virtual machine model.
windows.note: Plainly outside the product: there is no OS selection at all, isolates run inside V8, not a Windows or Linux guest OS chosen by the user.

macos.quote: Instead of creating a virtual machine for each function, an isolate is created within an existing environment. This model eliminates the cold starts of the virtual machine model.
macos.note: Same reasoning as windows: no macOS guest OS option exists for a V8-isolate execution product.

arm64.quote: V8 orchestrates isolates: lightweight contexts that provide your code with variables it can access and a safe environment to be executed within.
arm64.note: CPU architecture is fully abstracted by V8/Wasm; Cloudflare does not expose an ARM64 vs x86 choice to Workers/WfP customers.

self_host.quote: Rather than running on an individual's machine... Workers functions run on Cloudflare's global network - a growing global network of thousands of machines distributed across hundreds of locations.
self_host.note: Workers for Platforms is a managed Cloudflare-network-only product; there is no way to run the WfP dispatch/runtime infrastructure on your own infrastructure (workerd being open source does not make the WfP hosted product self-hostable).

byoc.quote: Workers functions run on Cloudflare's global network - a growing global network of thousands of machines distributed across hundreds of locations.
byoc.note: No bring-your-own-cloud/account option; Workers for Platforms only runs on Cloudflare's own network, not in a customer's AWS/GCP/Azure account.

live_resize.note: Memory (128 MB) and CPU-time limits are fixed platform limits (CPU-time cap is configurable per-Worker at deploy time up to 5 min, but there is no live/runtime resizing of a running isolate's resources).

usage_api.quote: In the dashboard, this appears as Metrics > Errors > Invocation Statuses. In analytics and Logpush, the invocation outcome is exceededCpu
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Cloudflare Workers and Workers for Platforms expose usage metrics (requests, CPU-ms) in the dashboard and via Logpush (for logs), but do not provide a programmatic REST API to query billable usage per-Worker or per-isolate. No usage or billing endpoint exists in the Cloudflare REST API for Workers resources; usage data is account-only via the dashboard/invoicing system.

locations_quote: Every service runs in every data center... 348 cities · 8 regions... Cloudflare will only use data centers that are physically located within the specified region to decrypt and service HTTPS traffic.
